overview: ANZ Group Holdings Limited (ANZGHL) is the non-operating holding company (since a January 2023 scheme of arrangement) for Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Limited (ANZBGL), one of Australia's 'Big Four' banks and the largest bank in New Zealand by some measures. The group provides retail, commercial and institutional banking across Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific, with an institutional banking network spanning 29 markets including Asia, Europe and the Americas. ANZ.NZ is the NZX-listed line of the ASX-primary-listed ANZGHL (ticker ANZ on ASX); the company reports in AUD while the NZX quote trades in NZD. Fiscal year ends 30 September.

business_model.summary: ANZ earns the large majority of its income from net interest margin on loans (mortgages, business and institutional lending) funded by customer deposits and wholesale debt, supplemented by fee, markets/trading and transaction banking income. FY2025: net interest income $17.9bn (~82% of operating income) vs other operating income (cash) $4.0bn (~18%). Revenue is recurring/spread-based rather than project-based, though Markets (trading) income is more volatile. Customer base spans mass-market retail/mortgage customers, SME and large commercial/agribusiness clients, high-net-worth individuals, and large corporate/institutional/government clients (via Transaction Banking, Corporate Finance and Markets).

revenue_streams.name: Australia Retail (mortgages, cards, deposits)
revenue_streams.note: cash profit $1,048m FY25 of $5,931m group total

revenue_streams.name: Suncorp Bank (Australia retail/commercial/agri, acquired 31-Jul-2024)
revenue_streams.note: cash profit $418m FY25, first full year

revenue_streams.name: Group Centre (Treasury, minority Asia investments, corporate costs)
revenue_streams.note: cash loss $1,097m FY25 incl. PT Panin impairment and redundancy charges

business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2C (retail mortgage/deposit customers, ~1.2m+ ANZ Plus digital customers) and B2B (SME, large commercial, institutional, government, agribusiness)
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia (~65-70% of profit incl. Suncorp), New Zealand (~27% of cash profit, ~$2.16bn of ~$5.9bn geographic profit), Rest of World/Pacific/Asia/Europe/Americas (~14% or ~$840m) per FY2025 geographic profit split (Australia $2,933m, New Zealand $2,158m, Rest of world $840m, cash basis)

main_competitors: Bendigo & Adelaide Bank / regional and non-bank/fintech lenders
competitive_position.market_position: One of Australia's Big Four banks (oligopoly controlling ~70% of Australian banking system assets); post-Suncorp acquisition, ANZ is roughly the #3 or #4 Australian home loan lender with ~14% share (behind CBA ~25%, Westpac ~21%); ANZ is also a market-leading bank in New Zealand and has the largest, most internationally networked Institutional franchise of the Australian majors

moat_factors.description: APRA/RBNZ prudential licensing, capital and compliance requirements create very high barriers for new entrants; Big Four oligopoly structure has persisted for decades
Domestic Systemically Important Bank (D-SIB) status and large stable deposit base ($749bn FY25) provide lower wholesale funding costs than smaller lenders
Diversified across Australia, NZ, Institutional and Pacific; leading Institutional/transaction banking franchise across 29 markets differentiates ANZ from domestically-focused peers
Banking relationships, direct debits and business banking integration create customer inertia, though mortgage refinancing has become easier and more price-competitive
Historically strong brand, but recent NFR failures, the ASIC bond-trading/retail misconduct penalties and APRA enforceable undertaking have damaged trust and invited heightened scrutiny

weaknesses: Weakest net interest margin trajectory among majors due to aggressive mortgage price competition
Lower ROE (~9-10%) than domestic peers reflecting lower-margin Institutional mix and higher costs
Significant non-financial risk/compliance failures requiring remediation spend and management distraction
Complexity and execution risk from integrating a large acquisition (Suncorp) while simultaneously restructuring the base business
Cost-to-income ratio rose sharply (58.2% FY25 cash, up from 51.3%) due to Suncorp, restructuring and remediation costs

growth_drivers: Suncorp Bank acquisition (completed 31 July 2024) — full-year contribution from FY2025, accelerated integration/migration to ANZ platform targeted for June 2027, with annual run-rate cost synergies raised from $260m to ~$500m by FY2029

ANZ Plus digital banking platform — over 1.2 million customers by mid-2025, driving lower cost-to-serve and new-to-bank customer acquisition; plan to migrate Suncorp and legacy retail/business customers onto a single ANZ Digital Platform

Institutional payments/platforms business (Transactive Global roll-out across Asia) — market-leading relationship-strength position, cross-border and trade/FX flows benefiting from geopolitical realignment and supply-chain diversification

New CEO Nuno Matos' 2030 strategy and 'four pillars' (Customer First, Simplicity, Resilience, Delivering value) — cost reset (~3,500 role reductions/~1,000 contractor reductions by Sept 2026), targeting ~3% total cost reduction in FY2026 and improved CTI

Capital return/franking improvement — franking on dividends increased from 70% to 75% in H1-2026, reflecting improved Australian geography earnings mix; potential resumption of buybacks once Suncorp integration capital needs are clearer
Rate-cycle tailwinds — replicating portfolio/capital hedge earnings benefit as rates normalize; margin pressure expected to moderate as competitive intensity in mortgages stabilizes

business.description: Group NIM fell to 1.54% in FY2025 (from 1.57%) driven by intense mortgage and deposit pricing competition among the majors; further RBA/RBNZ rate cuts could pressure deposit margins
Home loans are the largest single asset class; Australia Retail net loans $348.8bn plus Suncorp/NZ mortgage books make the group highly geared to Australasian house prices and household leverage
Aggressive discounting by CBA, Westpac, NAB and non-bank lenders compresses asset margins across Retail and Commercial
Gross impaired assets rose 50% YoY to $2,538m in FY2025, individually assessed impairment charges up sharply in Institutional, Commercial (Agri/SME) and Suncorp commercial property books

financial.description: CET1 ratio of 12.0-12.4% must be maintained well above APRA D-SIB minimums; capital consumed by Suncorp integration, remediation and buyback suspension reduces near-term flexibility
~$265.7bn wholesale funding instruments and reliance on term wholesale issuance ($36.7bn issued FY2025) expose the group to funding market conditions and credit spread volatility
Cross-currency earnings translation (NZ, Pacific, Asia, Europe operations) and economic hedge volatility affect statutory vs cash profit reconciliation

regulatory.risk: APRA Court Enforceable Undertaking (CEU) and Root Cause Remediation Plan
regulatory.description: In April 2025 ANZ entered a CEU with APRA over non-financial risk management and risk culture; a Root Cause Remediation Plan was submitted 30 September 2025; ongoing execution risk and potential for additional capital overlays or further APRA action if remediation milestones are missed

regulatory.risk: ASIC bond-trading and retail misconduct penalties
regulatory.description: ANZ admitted unconscionable conduct in a $14bn AOFM bond issuance (April 2023) including inflated bond trading volume reporting, plus widespread retail misconduct affecting ~65,000 customers; Federal Court ordered $250m in combined penalties (Dec 2025) versus the originally proposed $240m settlement; reputational damage and heightened supervisory scrutiny persist
Acquisition approval carried undertakings (e.g., Queensland-related commitments); accelerated migration timeline to June 2027 raises execution and conduct-risk exposure during system consolidation
Customer remediation charges recur across divisions (Retail, Commercial, NZ); financial crime and scams compliance investment is a rising structural cost

macro.description: Falling RBA/RBNZ policy rates reduce earnings on the replicating/hedge portfolio and deposit margins even as they support borrower serviceability

A sharp economic slowdown would increase credit impairment charges, particularly in Commercial/Agri and mortgage books already showing early stress (rising restructured home loans, gross impaired assets)

US tariff policy, US-China tensions and supply chain decoupling create volatility for the large Institutional/trade finance franchise and Asian minority investments (e.g., PT Panin impairment in FY2025)

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian and NZ banking sectors are mature, concentrated oligopolies (Big Four ~70% of Australian system assets) with modest single-digit credit growth; sector earnings currently pressured by margin compression from mortgage/deposit competition, partially offset by resilient credit quality and cost-cutting/technology investment across all majors
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - banks are geared to the credit and economic cycle (impairment charges rise in downturns) but ANZ's diversified retail/commercial/institutional/NZ mix smooths some volatility; Markets/trading income adds an additional layer of cyclicality tied to volatility and client activity
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High and two-sided - net interest margin depends on the spread between asset and deposit pricing and the yield on the replicating (capital hedge) portfolio; falling rates in 2025-26 have been a modest net NIM headwind, while a stable-to-rising rate environment typically supports margins
key_input_costs: Deposit costs (competition for at-call and term deposits)

recent_developments.event: Nuno Matos commenced as CEO (12 May 2025), succeeding Shayne Elliott who retired after ~9 years; new 2030 strategy unveiled around four pillars (Customer First, Simplicity, Resilience, Delivering value)
ANZ entered a court enforceable undertaking (CEU) with APRA over non-financial risk management and risk culture shortcomings

ANZ agreed to a $240m ASIC settlement (later confirmed by Federal Court at $250m combined penalties, judgment Dec-2025) over bond-trading misconduct in a $14bn government bond issuance and widespread retail misconduct affecting ~65,000 customers
Announced restructuring: ~3,500 roles and ~1,000 contractor engagements to be cut by September 2026; pre-tax restructuring charge of $579m ($408m after tax) recognised in H2 FY2025
October 2025 Strategy Day: accelerated Suncorp Bank migration timeline to June 2027 (from a later original date) and raised expected annual cost synergies to ~$500m by FY2029 (from $260m originally)

FY2025 full year results: cash profit down 13% to $5,931m (statutory down $560m to $6,035m); CET1 12.0% (pro-forma 12.26% after ceasing ~$800m remaining buyback and returning ~$1bn surplus NOHC capital); final dividend 83cps (FY25 total 166cps, 70% franked)
Federal Court formally ordered $250m combined penalties against ANZ (up from the $240m proposed settlement) for the bond-trading and retail misconduct matters

H1-2026 results (half ended 31 March 2026): statutory profit $3,650m, cash profit $3,780m (up 70% HoH, +14% ex significant items); CET1 rose to 12.39% (+36bps); interim dividend maintained at 83cps but franking increased to 75% (from 70%)
Bloomberg reporting increased investor pressure on CEO Nuno Matos to shift focus from cost-cutting toward revenue/growth delivery as the cost-reset program matures

guidance.as_of: H1-2026 Results (May 2026) / FY2025 Results (Nov 2025) / October 2025 Strategy Day

items.notes: Management targeting a cost reset following FY2025 restructuring (~3,500 role cuts, ~1,000 contractor reductions) to be substantially complete by September 2026
Increased from original $260m estimate at acquisition; vast majority to be captured in FY2028; total integration costs estimated at $745m ($300m incurred to date as of late 2025)
Brought forward from original later timeline; ~34% of customer migration complete by end of March 2026
CFO flagged headwinds from further rate cuts and continued mortgage/deposit competition, though management expects competitive intensity to moderate over the medium term

items.target: Interim dividend maintained at 83 cps; franking raised to 75%
items.notes: On-market buyback ceased in FY2025 (final ~$800m tranche stopped); ~$1bn of surplus NOHC capital returned to the Bank rather than shareholders; future buyback resumption not yet reinstated as of H1-2026

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Nuno Matos has emphasised safe, sustainable, on-time execution of five immediate priorities and progress on the Root Cause Remediation Plan required under the APRA enforceable undertaking. Management describes FY2025-26 as a 'cost reset' phase, with increasing investor pressure (per Bloomberg, April 2026) to pivot toward revenue growth and demonstrate that cost discipline translates into durable returns once the restructuring and Suncorp integration programs mature.

bull_case: Suncorp Bank integration is tracking ahead of plan with synergy estimates nearly doubled (to ~$500m/year) and an accelerated migration timeline, providing a multi-year earnings tailwind as integration costs roll off after FY2027-28

H1-2026 results show a strong rebound (cash profit +14% ex significant items, CET1 up to 12.39%) suggesting FY2025's remediation/restructuring charges were largely one-off and underlying earnings momentum is recovering

New CEO-led cost reset (~3,500 roles cut, ~3% FY26 cost reduction target) and ANZ Plus digital platform scaling (1.2m+ customers) should structurally lower the cost-to-income ratio over the medium term
Well-capitalised (CET1 ~12.4%, above regulatory minimums) with a diversified, internationally networked Institutional franchise that differentiates ANZ from domestically-focused Australian peers
Improving franking (70%→75%) and a stable ~4.7% dividend yield provide attractive income support while the market waits for the cost/integration story to play out
bear_case: Serious non-financial risk failures (APRA enforceable undertaking, $250m Federal Court penalty for bond-trading/retail misconduct) signal deep-seated risk-culture problems that could trigger further regulatory action, remediation costs, or reputational damage
Net interest margin remains under structural pressure from aggressive mortgage and deposit competition among the Big Four, capping revenue growth even as costs are cut

Execution risk is high: simultaneously running a large cost-reduction program, integrating Suncorp Bank (accelerated to June 2027), and delivering a multi-year Root Cause Remediation Plan increases the chance of missteps, and a new CEO (from May 2025) adds leadership transition risk

ROE/ROTE (~9-10%) lags historical levels and domestic peers, and cost-to-income ratio spiked to 58.2% in FY2025 (from 51.3%), raising questions about whether targeted cost savings will be sufficient to restore returns

Rising credit impairment signals (gross impaired assets +50% YoY, higher individually assessed charges in Commercial/Agri and Suncorp commercial property) could worsen if the Australian/NZ economy weakens, while buyback suspension reduces near-term capital return upside
